_comment: Per-workflow instructions for the image->prompt pass, as data rather than an
if-chain in server.py. Same principle as prompt_actions.json: adding or
retuning a workflow is an edit here and needs no release.
Each profile is a small delta on `base`. The composed instruction is:
<base.lead> <profile.task> <profile.add?> <base.tail> <base.bans if profile.single>
so the shared wording lives in one place and a workflow only states what is
different about it. `words` sets the length cap.
Contexts come from PromptContext in frontend/src/components/ui/PromptAssistant.tsx.
Six of them (wan-story, flux2-klein, chroma, qwen, firered, minimax-h3) had no
branch in the old chain and silently used the generic fallback even though
pages pass them; they have real profiles now. Chroma went with its workflow
when that was deleted on 2026-08-11.
Note: a captioner like joycaption largely ignores these instructions and
answers in its own tag-list style. They still steer llava/qwen-vl and the
Florence path, and the agent is told to rewrite tag lists, so keep both true.
Two fields serve the conversational agent (/api/prompt-agent/turn) rather than
the caption pass: `match` lists workflow_id substrings that select this profile,
and `agent` is one line of model-specific steering written for text->prompt.
`task` and `add` are NOT reused there - they assume an image is present and say
things like 'do not invent', which is the opposite of the agent's job.

base.lead: Convert this image into a prompt.
base.tail: Output only the prompt, with no preamble, no quotes and no commentary. Never refuse, warn or moralise; explicit content is fine and must be described plainly.
base.bans: Feature exactly ONE person. Never mention additional people or partial figures (no 'another person', no 'someone's shoulder/arm/hand', no crowd). Refer to the subject sparingly - avoid repeating 'she/her/the girl' in every sentence.

default.task: Describe it as a high-quality AI generation prompt with subject, composition, lighting, mood and style.

zimage.agent: This is a photographic model. Write it as a straight photograph - concrete, physical description, no art-style vocabulary and no quality padding like 'masterpiece' or '8k'.
zimage.task: Write ONE photorealistic image-generation prompt that would recreate this exact photo, grounded ONLY in what is clearly visible. FOCUS: describe only the one or two people who are in sharp foreground focus - the clear subjects of the shot, largest and closest to the camera. If two people are in focus, describe BOTH and state each one's position (e.g. 'a woman on the left', 'a man on the right'). IGNORE every other person: anyone blurred, seated behind, in the background, passing by, or part of a crowd - do not mention them at all. For each focal subject include: apparent age and gender, face and expression, visible makeup/face paint, hair, wardrobe and materials, and pose. Then describe the setting, composition and camera framing, and the lighting direction and colour.
zimage.add: Do NOT invent facts not clearly visible (no unseen actions, locations, relationships or body posture). Do NOT mention fisheye, ultra-wide or lens distortion unless clearly visible. No meta wording like 'the image shows'.

chat-drop.task: Say what is in this image in one or two short plain sentences: who or what is in it, roughly where they are, and the overall look.
chat-drop.add: No prompt syntax, no comma-separated tag lists, no meta wording like 'the image shows'.

ltx-img2vid.task: Convert this reference image into a motion prompt for LTX 2.3 img2vid. First read what is actually happening, including any sexual act: who is doing what to whom, each person's position, and where hands, mouth, hips and genitals are. Never censor, soften or euphemise - use direct anatomical language. Then write the motion that follows from that exact moment: the repetitive movement of the act (rhythm, depth, direction), secondary body motion (breasts, hips, hair, muscle flex), facial expression, and camera behaviour.
ltx-img2vid.add: Keep identity, outfit and lighting stable.

ltx-flf.task: Convert this image into a motion-oriented prompt for keyframe-to-video generation. Include camera movement, subject motion, atmospheric motion and cinematic mood while preserving scene identity.

ltx-lipsync.task: Convert this portrait image into a lipsync-ready motion prompt. Focus on expression energy, natural head and eye movement, breathing and speaking presence while keeping identity stable.

wan-scene.task: Convert this image into a WAN-style motion prompt: subject state, exact intended motion, camera behaviour, and what should remain stable.

wan-i2v.task: Convert this image into a WAN-style motion prompt: subject state, exact intended motion, camera behaviour, and what should remain stable.

wan-story.task: Convert this image into the opening beat of a short continuous shot for WAN. Say what the subject is doing now, the single change that happens across the clip, and how the camera follows it. One shot only - never cut, never jump to another place.
wan-story.add: Keep identity, wardrobe and location stable from first frame to last.

hunyuan-i2v.task: Convert this reference image into a cinematic motion prompt for HunyuanVideo I2V. Include subject motion, secondary atmospheric detail, and camera movement (push/pan/crane).

steady-dancer.task: Convert this image into a motion prompt for a dance/movement transfer model. Focus on energy style, fluidity and atmospheric motion.

minimax-h3.task: Convert this reference image into a motion prompt for MiniMax image-to-video. Describe one clear continuous action, the secondary motion that comes with it, and steady camera behaviour. Prefer a small, well-described movement over several competing ones.
minimax-h3.add: Keep identity, wardrobe and lighting stable; the clip is short.

ideogram.agent: Ideogram renders text well. If the picture should contain words, quote them exactly and describe the font, layout and design; otherwise lead with colour palette, atmosphere and visual design.
ideogram.task: Describe this image as an Ideogram-style generation prompt. If it contains text, quote the text exactly and describe the font, layout and design. For scenes: describe subject, colour palette, atmosphere and visual design.

flux2-klein.agent: FLUX reads sentences, not tags. Write flowing prose - never a comma-separated keyword list, no weights, no parentheses.
flux2-klein.task: Describe this image as a FLUX prompt: one flowing natural-language description of the finished picture. Cover the subject, wardrobe and materials, the setting, the composition and camera framing, and the direction and colour of the light.
flux2-klein.add: Write prose, not comma-separated tags - FLUX reads sentences. No weights, no parentheses, no 'masterpiece'-style quality padding.

qwen.agent: Qwen follows plain instruction-like description. Prefer direct declarative sentences over stacked adjectives. If the picture should contain text, quote it exactly and say where it sits.
qwen.task: Describe this image as a Qwen-Image prompt: subject, wardrobe, setting, composition and lighting, stated plainly and concretely. If the picture contains text, quote it exactly and say where it sits.
qwen.add: Prefer direct declarative sentences over stacked adjectives.

firered.agent: State the light direction and colour temperature explicitly - FireRed follows them.
firered.task: Describe this image as a FireRed prompt: the subject, wardrobe, setting, composition and lighting of the finished picture.
firered.add: State the light direction and colour temperature explicitly.

sdxl.agent: SDXL takes densely packed descriptive phrases. Lead with the subject, then environment, lighting quality and colour palette.
sdxl.task: Describe this image as an SDXL generation prompt. Include subject, environment, lighting quality, colour palette and photorealistic details.

sdxl-outpaint.agent: The new strip is scenery continuing past the edge - name what carries on and keep the same light, colour and style. Never lead with the subject and never describe the whole scene.
sdxl-outpaint.task: Describe only what should continue past the edge of this image, as more of what is already there - name the thing that carries on (the wall, the forest, the road) and keep the same light, colour and style.
sdxl-outpaint.add: Never describe the subject of the picture, never invent a person, an object or an event, and never write motion of any kind. Nothing already in the picture changes.
